title: Rhubarb and Ginger Jam
subtitle: Sharp spring rhubarb with warm ginger, a classic British combination
excerpt: Forced rhubarb in early spring gives a vivid pink jam; outdoor rhubarb from April onward goes deeper and more tart. Ginger brings warmth and sits cleanly against the acidity. Makes about three 450 g jars.
sourceNotes: Mrs Beeton (PG #10136); Pam Corbin, Preserves. Rhubarb is low in pectin and needs lemon juice; the ginger-rhubarb combination is a Victorian British preserve classic.

recipe.freezeNotes: Raw chopped rhubarb freezes well — straight into the bag, no blanching needed.
recipe.batchNotes: Up to 1.5 kg rhubarb at once.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Macerate the rhubarb in sugar overnight to extract juice and reduce cooking time.

glossaryTerms.definition: To steep fruit in sugar or liquid to draw out juice and soften the texture. For jam, this also partly dissolves the sugar before cooking begins.

content.text: Rhubarb and ginger jam is a spring staple,  sharp fruit with a kick of warmth from the ginger root. Rhubarb has very little natural pectin, so it needs lemon juice to help the set, and it benefits from macerating overnight before cooking, which pulls out the juice and keeps the pieces intact. Makes about three 450 g jars.

Layer the rhubarb, sugar, grated ginger, and lemon juice in a bowl. Cover and leave at room temperature for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight. The sugar will draw juice from the rhubarb and partly dissolve.

d fruit into the jam pan and stir over low heat until the sugar has completely dissolved. Raise to a full rolling boil and cook for 15 to 20 minutes, testing on a cold plate from 15 minutes. Rhubarb is slow to set,  be patient. When the surface wrinkles, take off the heat, skim, rest 5 minutes, then jar.

items.cause: Rhubarb's low pectin combined with overripe or late-season stalks.
items.fix: Add the juice of another lemon and 1 tsp pectin, return to the boil, test after 5 minutes.

items.cause: Prolonged high heat can dull the ginger heat.
items.fix: Add a third of the ginger at the end of cooking, off the heat, to preserve brightness.

items.cause: Outdoor rhubarb is sharper than forced rhubarb.
items.fix: Increase the sugar by 50 g or reduce lemon juice by 1 tbsp next time.

items.cause: Rhubarb was not macerating long enough, and the long cook broke it down.
items.fix: Overnight maceration firms the fruit and reduces cooking time. The jam will still taste good with a soft texture.

content.text: 12 months sealed. Refrigerate once opened and use within 4 weeks.
